# Real-hardware golden dumps

`results_hw.txt` was captured from **real MCPX APU silicon** (original Xbox
console) via the xbtest hardware oracle. It contains one canonical difftest
dump per corpus case; `check_goldens.py` (one level up) diffs the JIT
emulator against these goldens offline, with no console attached.

## Capture details

- Capture date: 2026-08-23
- Oracle: xbtest, driven by `client/run_corpus_hw.py` from the same
  checkout as the XBE on the console
- DSP core: **GP** (plain RAM in X/Y, no ROM region)
- Corpus: the committed `corpus.lod` / `corpus.meta` in this directory
  (generated by `corpus.py` at the revision that added these goldens);
  `MANIFEST.sha256` binds goldens and corpus together
- Execution model: one fresh boot per case; the boot image is a register
  init preamble + the corpus P image + a `jmp <snapshot>` patched at the
  case's end PC, so cases 1..k execute sequentially exactly as the JIT
  steps them (inter-slot gaps are NOPs)
- Emulator boot profile: `difftest corpus ... --boot=hw` (OMR=$30F and
  VBA=$FF0000 mirror silicon boot values; rewriting them on hardware
  risks remapping memory/vectors, so the runner leaves them alone)

## Comparison caveats baked into the goldens

- `ssh`/`ssl` are recorded as `-` (unknown, skipped by diff.py) whenever a
  case ends with an empty stack (sp=0): reading SSH pops the stack and an
  empty-stack pop is undefined on silicon (and hard-asserts in the
  embedder's interpreter). They are real values for cases ending with sp != 0.
- `a2`/`b2` are normalized to the raw 8-bit register value: the silicon
  read path (`move a2, x:`) sign-extends into the 24-bit store.
- `steps`/`cyc` are absent: hardware runs free (uncounted); diff.py treats
  them as informational anyway.
- `pc` is the case's end PC; the per-case magic-word handshake proves
  execution actually reached it.

## Regenerating

Only regenerate when the corpus changes and a console is available:

```
# on a machine that can reach the console (see xbtest repo)
python3 tools/difftest/corpus.py
python3 $XBTEST/client/run_corpus_hw.py tools/difftest/out/corpus.lod \
    tools/difftest/out/corpus.meta --out tools/difftest/goldens/results_hw.txt
cp tools/difftest/out/corpus.{lod,meta} tools/difftest/goldens/
cd tools/difftest/goldens && sha256sum corpus.lod corpus.meta results_hw.txt > MANIFEST.sha256
```

Update the capture date above when you do.

Recaptured 2026-08-24 with `--dump-mem --dump-stack`: results now carry
the X/Y/P memory end-state and the 15 hardware stack slots per case
(sh/sl keys from the stack-walk epilogue). Corpus image and sealed
fingerprint unchanged; registers match the prior capture.
